name: Jaimie Branch
label: International Anthem
lede: Jaimie Branch went to hear improvised music at Chicago's Velvet Lounge as a teenager, rebuilt her life in Brooklyn, and led Fly or Die, a quartet whose first album made NPR Music's Top 50 of 2017. Her last one, a Pitchfork Best New Album, came out a year after she died.

eras.title: Long Island to the Chicago suburbs
eras.text: Born in Huntington, New York, Branch starts on piano at three and trumpet at nine, then moves to Wilmette, Illinois at fourteen and starts going into Chicago to hear improvised music and rock.

years.src: NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary · Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Jaimie Branch is born in Huntington, New York
years.p: Piano at three, trumpet at nine, per NPR's obituary.
years.xp:
NPR says she later studied at the New England Conservatory in Boston with Charles Schlueter, a Boston Symphony principal trumpeter, and with improvisers [[Joe Morris|a9527992-99db-46c3-a2aa-abab9c36e90e]] and John McNeil.

She worked on circular breathing and multiphonics, extended techniques that let one trumpet sound like more than one voice.

years.src: NPR: Chicago trumpeter jaimie branch delivers · The Quietus
years.h: A Wilmette teenager hangs around Velvet Lounge and Lounge Ax
years.p: Her family settles in Wilmette, Illinois, and at fourteen she starts heading into Chicago for improvised music and rock, per NPR's local station.
years.xp:
Velvet Lounge was a free-jazz club and Lounge Ax a rock club, a few miles apart. NPR's Chicago coverage of her second album has her in both as a teenager.

The Quietus later put her sound in a Chicago mix of free jazz, punk, blues, hip hop, house and West African traditions, alongside her Colombian heritage.

eras.title: Chicago sessions, a Baltimore detour
eras.text: Back from Boston, she plays with Ken Vandermark and Nicole Mitchell, tries grad school in Baltimore, and ends up in Brooklyn.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Her first credit is on bassist Jason Ajemian's The Art of Dying
years.p: Wikipedia lists her on [[Jason Ajemian|c9fd3164-ef5e-4a91-b1da-ef7ee96ddba2]]'s 2006 record, the start of a partnership that runs through every Fly or Die album.
years.xp: Ajemian and Branch were both in Chicago's improvised-music scene. He plays bass in every Fly or Die lineup, and he is one of the voices in the band's 2023 statement remembering her.

years.src: NPR: Chicago trumpeter jaimie branch delivers · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: She moves back to Chicago for good
years.p: NPR dates the return to 2007, and she plays on Keefe Jackson's Just Like This the same year.
years.xp: NPR's obituary also has her at the Festival of New Trumpet Music that year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Princess, Princess gives her a trio of her own
years.p: With bassist Toby Summerfield and drummer Frank Rosaly. The same year she plays on drummer Tim Daisy's 1000 Lights.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: Vandermark's Predella Group puts her beside Jeff Parker and Jeb Bishop
years.p: [[Ken Vandermark|e5a4107f-5bb3-4f24-b9b7-927bb23840b5]]'s band has guitarist [[Jeff Parker|4894f8eb-be75-4bd5-a3a3-7c20894439f9]] and trombonist Jeb Bishop in it, and Branch takes the trumpet chair.
years.xp: She also played with [[Nicole Mitchell|56f280d6-2f91-4af8-8a1a-fde9c9f2b876]] and had an early trio with cellist Fred Lonberg-Holm, per NPR. Wikipedia says she worked as a sound engineer and organizer around the same scene.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: She leaves Towson after two years, and starts a label first
years.p: She enrolls at Towson University in Baltimore and launches Pionic Records to release her group Bomb Shelter.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says that six months after leaving Towson she moved to New York to seek treatment for heroin addiction. NPR's obituary says she relocated to Brooklyn around 2014 after treatment for substance use disorder.

The two sources differ on timing: Wikipedia dates the Brooklyn move to spring 2015.

years.src: Wikipedia: International Anthem
years.h: A live-jazz series at a Chicago bar becomes International Anthem
years.p: Drummer Scottie McNiece and engineer David Allen turn it into a label. First release: [[Rob Mazurek|73c34525-f9c6-4c33-9abe-007748aaebe5]]'s Alternative Moon Cycles.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, McNiece and Allen founded the label in 2012 and launched it officially in 2014. Gilles Peterson named it his Label of the Year in 2020.

Allen would later mix and master Branch's final album.

eras.title: Fly or Die
eras.text: In Brooklyn she plays on other people's records until a one-off set with three Chicago friends catches the ear of a label co-founder. The first Fly or Die album lands in NPR Music's Top 50 of 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · Bandcamp Daily · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
years.h: She lands in Brooklyn and plays on everyone's records
years.p: Fred Lonberg-Holm, Mike Pride, Luke Stewart and Jason Nazary, plus albums by Never Enough Hope, Local H and the Atlas Moth.
years.xp: Bandcamp Daily adds James Brandon Lewis's Unruly Quintet, C'est Trois, and guest spots on albums by TV on the Radio and Talib Kweli. NPR says she lived in Red Hook.

years.big: "I thought it was gonna be a one-off. I had no idea what was in store."
years.src: The Quietus · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: Scottie McNiece hears the first Fly or Die set and asks for a record
years.p: Branch told The Quietus about the night she played graphic scores with bassist Jason Ajemian, drummer Chad Taylor and cellist [[Tomeka Reid|d91d6fca-ea9c-4a5d-a0ba-5a666c81cd51]], with McNiece listening.
years.xp:
The Quietus reports the band started in 2015, five or six months before the recording. The scores mix traditional notation, text, drawings and color coding, so the players can find a section without reading a wall of paper.

Branch listened back to that first set and pulled the themes that became 'theme 001' and 'the storm' on the debut. The other three were Chicago transplants too.

years.src: The Quietus
years.h: Anteloper begins when a third player doesn't show
years.p: Branch and drummer [[Jason Nazary|49a03c33-526e-46f9-b992-5b60c994b1ec]] both arrive with electronics, and find they're a duo.
years.xp:
She told The Quietus: "Fly Or Die is my right hand, Anteloper is my left hand." Anteloper is the electronic project, and Fly or Die is almost entirely acoustic.

She uses hardware synths, effects pedals and loopers, while Nazary works with modular and trigger setups.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · Stereogum: Remembering · NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary
yt: Full set at HOlO, Queens, April 16, 2018
years.h: Fly or Die makes NPR Music's Top 50 of 2017
years.p: Branch's first album under her own name, on International Anthem: trumpet, voice, Reid's cello, Ajemian's bass, Taylor's drums.
years.xp:
Guests include Matt Schneider, Ben LaMar Gay and Josh Berman, per Wikipedia.

A Stereogum column remembering Branch after her death says its writer still stands by his pick of it as the best jazz album of 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Anteloper's Kudu arrives on International Anthem
years.p: The first record from Branch and drummer Nazary's electro-acoustic duo.

years.cap: Branch on trumpet in Mars Williams's An Ayler Xmas band, Club W71, Weikersheim, Germany, December 2018
years.src: NPR: Chicago trumpeter jaimie branch delivers
yt: Radio concert at BIMHUIS, Amsterdam, Nov 8, 2018
years.h: A rant improvised in Paris becomes 'prayer for amerikkka'
years.p: NPR says what she shouted on stage there became the core of the political song on her next album. She then quits her day job to play full time.
years.xp: The year was also full of European dates. A BIMHUIS radio concert in Amsterdam on November 8 is on video, and that December she played trumpet in Mars Williams's An Ayler Xmas band in Weikersheim, Germany.

eras.title: Bird dogs and alarms
eras.text: Cellist Lester St. Louis arrives, the politics get louder, and Fly or Die II reaches the top 10 of the 2019 Jazz Critics Poll. A live album and a Red Hook festival set follow in 2021.

years.big: "It's a big f-you to all those people."
q: The trumpet is an alert, and we're sounding some alarms.
years.src: NPR: Chicago trumpeter jaimie branch delivers · The Quietus
years.h: 'prayer for amerikkka' takes aim at the prisons on the border
years.p: That's how Branch described the song to NPR's Chicago station. It was inspired by a family her social worker mother assisted.
years.xp:
On the border prisons she told The Quietus: "It wasn't a song about Trump." Biden was in office by then, she said, and the prisons were still there.

She explained the spelling as a comment on the nation's foundations, and said in the NPR interview that the trumpet is an alert, and the band was sounding some alarms.

years.cap: Branch at Jazzfestival Saalfelden, Austria, August 2019
years.src: NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary · The Quietus
yt: theme 001, live at Moods, Zurich, Jan 23 2020
years.h: Cellist Lester St. Louis takes Tomeka Reid's chair
years.p: NPR says the record, Fly or Die II: Bird Dogs of Paradise, reached the top 10 of the 2019 Jazz Critics Poll.
years.xp:
The Quietus says Branch had been obsessed with birds since childhood: "I've been a little obsessed with birds, since they're basically dinosaurs, right?" The covers of both Fly or Die albums show Colombian birds of paradise, a nod to her Colombian heritage.

She also traced part of it to a pet parakeet named Kiwi, and joked about it in the interview.
play: Fly or Die II: Bird Dogs of Paradise

years.p: The set at Pioneer Works, in Branch's own neighborhood, was filmed. Fly or Die Live also comes out on International Anthem this year.

eras.title: Omaha, then August
eras.text: A residency at the Bemis Center in Omaha, a third record with Jason Nazary, and Branch's death in Red Hook in August at 39.

years.cap: Branch with Fly or Die, Tivoli Vredenburg, Utrecht
years.src: The Fader · Bandcamp Daily · International Anthem
years.h: Omaha's Bemis Center hosts the quartet for a residency
years.p: The band records the next album there. Branch wants longer forms, more modulations, more noise, more singing, per the label.
years.xp:
The band's later statement says she always thought big. Per Bandcamp Daily, overdubs and mixing followed in July at International Anthem Studios in Chicago.

Ajemian told Bandcamp Daily: "There were a couple little things that were done afterward, but she was all over it."

years.src: Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch
years.h: Anteloper's Pink Dolphins is the duo's third LP
years.p: Branch and Nazary's third release as a duo.

years.cap: Branch with Fly or Die, Tivoli Vredenburg, Utrecht
years.src: NPR: jaimie branch trumpet obituary · Wikipedia: Jaimie Branch · Stereogum: Remembering
years.h: Branch dies at home in Red Hook at 39
years.p: International Anthem announces her death. Wikipedia states the cause as an accidental drug overdose; the label gave none, NPR reported at the time.
years.xp:
Her sister Kate Branch said she was "the bravest person I knew, on and off the stage." NPR also quotes trumpeter Dave Douglas: "She brought us so many insights into how the trumpet could engage in the music differently."

A Stereogum writer said the news hit the younger jazz scene like a sledgehammer to the sternum.

eras.title: The record she left
eras.text: The album was recorded in April 2022 and finished that July, and International Anthem puts it out on schedule. Pitchfork names it Best New Album and Metacritic lists a 95.

years.src: The Fader · International Anthem
yt: take over the world, official video
years.h: International Anthem announces the last Fly or Die album
years.p: The band's statement says "jaimie never had small ideas. She always thought big." The lead single 'take over the world' gets a video directed by Jon Philpot.
years.xp: The statement adds that the more people told her something was too difficult, the more determined she got. It promised longer forms, more modulations, more noise and more singing.

years.cap: Cover of Fly or Die Fly or Die Fly or Die ((world war)), International Anthem, IARC0066
years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Fly or Die Fly or Die Fly or Die · International Anthem
years.h: The last album gets an 8.5 and Best New Album from Pitchfork
years.p: Andy Cush's review earned it Best New Album, and the site ranked it No. 28 of 2023. It came out August 25.
years.xp:
Cush called it a heartbreaking glimpse of where she might have gone next and, more importantly, a joy to hear. Giovanni Russonello of the New York Times said it was as electrifying as the first two LPs, with a wider sonic horizon.

Metacritic lists 95 from ten reviews, The Guardian placed it No. 48 of 2023, and per Wikipedia it peaked at No. 20 on the UK Independent Albums chart.

It features Branch, Lester St. Louis, Jason Ajemian and Chad Taylor, plus trombonist Nick Broste, flutist Rob Frye and vocalist Akenya Seymour, per the label. David M. Allen mixed and mastered it.

years.h: Roulette hosts the release show, on film
years.p: The band celebrates the album at Roulette, and the night was filmed.
